title: Harmonize fluid anchor palette and shadow presets for responsive components
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Create a consolidated set of fluid color anchors, a refined responsive typography scale, and a compact set of shadow/elevation presets and radius tokens designed specifically for interactive components (buttons, inputs, table rows, charts). The goal is to reduce token variance across breakpoints, improve perceived depth consistency across scales, and ensure WCAG contrast for primary and interactive states while enabling easy runtime interpolation for responsive UI.
acceptance_criteria: A documented set of color anchors (neutral/primary/interactive/critical) with 5 ramp stops and CSS variables for fluid interpolation across breakpoints
A responsive type scale defined in steps with token names and recommended use cases (ui/small/body/heading) and a fallback mapping for legacy components
A spacing and radius token set with 4 responsive presets (compact, default, comfortable, expanded) and migration guide
A small set (4) of shadow/elevation presets tuned for 3 major viewport size ranges with examples applied to button, card, table-row, and tooltip
Cross-browser SASS/CSS examples and tokens exposed in the design tokens package and Figma library
Accessibility checklist: primary interactive color meets AA for normal text and 3:1 for UI components where required
Migration notes for engineering including a deprecation timeline for overlapping tokens
tasks: Audit current token usage across components: buttons, inputs, tables, charts (design/ENG collaboration)
Define color anchor ramps and name scheme (e.g., anchor-primary-xx)
Design shadow presets at 3 reference sizes and test in Figma with motion/blur adjustments
Create responsive typography scale with fluid clamp values and token mapping
Prototype runtime interpolation examples (CSS custom properties + small JS helper) and share with infra
Write migration guide and roll-out plan for Console and Design Kit consumers
Collect dev feedback in weekly sync and address edge cases (high-contrast mode, print styles)
Prepare PRD and handoff artifacts for release-2025.03
decisions: Adopt fluid anchors (CSS clamp) for large-to-small breakpoints instead of multiple discrete tokens to reduce duplication
Limit elevation presets to 4 (none/base/raised/floating) to simplify engineering surface and expectations
Introduce radius presets (r-0, r-1, r-2, r-loose) mapped to spacing scale so components can adapt consistently
Keep legacy static tokens for a deprecation window of 3 months and provide automated codemod suggestions
tradeoffs: Fluid anchors increase runtime complexity slightly (requires clamp() and variable math) but reduce long-term maintenance and token explosion
Fewer elevation presets can limit fine-grained control for visual designers but improves developer predictability and performance
Using anchor ramps means some corner cases will need per-component tinting adjustments (e.g., charts where precise color delta matters)
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Alvarez): prioritize token names that are stable for SDK exports; avoid semantic names that collide with product terminology
Engineering (Ravi Singh): prefer numeric suffix scheme for anchors (anchor-10..anchor-90) to make mapping to quantized palettes easier
Accessibility (Lena Morales): ensure interactive focus ring contrasts against both surface and foreground tokens; requested 3 sample alt palettes for testing
